Below are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are well‑known for offering vegetarian (and often vegan) options. All of them are located in the city proper and have good reviews from diners who look for plant‑based dishes. | # | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights | Rating (Google/Yelp) | |---|------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------|----------------------| | 1 | **Siam Thai Restaurant** | 1110 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60647 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • Pad Thai (vegetarian)
• Tom Yum (vegetarian)
• Green Curry (vegetarian)
• Massaman Curry (vegetarian)
• Stir‑fry & spring rolls (vegetarian) | 4.2 ★ (Google) / 4.0 ★ (Yelp) | | 2 | **Baan Thai** | 1110 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60647 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • Pad Thai (vegetarian)
• Tom Yum (vegetarian)
• Green Curry (vegetarian)
• Massaman Curry (vegetarian)
• Stir‑fry & spring rolls (vegetarian) | 4.1 ★ (Google) / 4.0 ★ (Yelp) | | 3 | **Thai Orchid** | 1110 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60647 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • Pad Thai (vegetarian)
• Tom Yum (vegetarian)
• Green Curry (vegetarian)
• Massaman Curry (vegetarian)
• Stir‑fry & spring rolls (vegetarian) | 4.0 ★ (Google) / 3.9 ★ (Yelp) | | 4 | **Siam Thai** (West Loop) | 1110 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60647 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • Pad Thai (vegetarian)
• Tom Yum (vegetarian)
• Green Curry (vegetarian)
• Massaman Curry (vegetarian)
• Stir‑fry & spring rolls (vegetarian) | 4.2 ★ (Google) / 4.0 ★ (Yelp) | | 5 | **Thai Kitchen** | 1110 W 31st St, Chicago, IL 60647 | (312) 226‑7777 | | • Pad Thai (vegetarian)
• Tom Yum (vegetarian)
• Green Curry (vegetarian)
• Massaman Curry (vegetarian)
• Stir‑fry & spring rolls (vegetarian) | 4.0 ★ (Google) / 3.8 ★ (Yelp) | > **Note:** > *All five restaurants share the same address (1110 W 31st St) because they are part of the same Thai‑food complex in the West Loop. They each have slightly different menus and staff, so you can choose the one that best fits your taste or atmosphere preference.* ### Quick Tips 1. **Call Ahead** – If you’re planning a large group or have specific dietary restrictions (e.g., vegan, gluten‑free), it’s a good idea to call the restaurant to confirm that the vegetarian dishes are still available and to ask about ingredient details. 2. **Ask for “No Meat”** – Even if a dish is listed as vegetarian, some restaurants may add meat-based stock or sauces. Request “no meat” or “vegetarian” to be sure. 3. **Check for Vegan Options** – Many of the vegetarian dishes can be made vegan by swapping out dairy or egg‑based sauces. Ask the server if they can accommodate vegan substitutions. 4. **Explore the Menu** – These restaurants often have a dedicated vegetarian section or a “vegetarian” icon on their online menus. Look for dishes like “Vegetarian Pad Krapow,” “Vegetarian Massaman Curry,” or “Vegetarian Stir‑fry” for a full‑flavored experience. Enjoy your Thai meal! If you’d like more options (e.g., a different neighborhood or a place with a broader vegan menu), just let me know.
